LESSON: PLAIN SCALE DRAWING

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8
Subject: FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT ENGLISH
Strand: Communication in Pre-Technical Studies
Topic 2.3: Plain Scale Drawing
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 6

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Plain Scale Drawing, part of Communication in Pre-Technical Studies in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / Grade 8 FOR LEARNERS WITH HEARING IMPAIRMENT ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: What is the importance of drawing figures to scale? 2. How are plane figures drawn to scale?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. sign terms related to plain scale drawing used in drawing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plain Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe the features of a plain scale used in drawing,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plain Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. interpret a plain scale used in drawing, • In purposive groups, learners are guided to watch a video or observe a demonstration on how to sign terms related to plain scale drawing used in drawing. • In pairs, learners are guided to use print media and digital devices to list, fingerspell and sign terms related to plain scale as used in drawing. 1. What is the importance of drawing figures to scale? 2. How are plane figures drawn to scale? 27

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plain Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. draw plane figures to a given scale,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plain Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. appreciate the use of plain scale drawing in the work environment. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print and non- print media to search for the meaning of plain scale as used in drawing. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to discuss the term plain scale as used in drawing. Ensure the discussions are based on bilingual communication to suit both the Hard of Hearing and deaf learners. • Learners to be guided to use print media and digital devices to search for information about the features of a plain scale, • In purposive groups, learners are guided to use print media and digital devices to search for instruments used to construct a plain scale. • In purposive groups, learners are guided to watch 28 a demonstration on how to use drawing instruments to construct a plain scale. • In pairs, learners are guided to use drawing instruments to construct a plain scale. Ensure the learner is provided with a one-on-one demonstration for this activity. • In pairs, learners are providing with a one-on- one demonstration on how to read plain scales. • Using appropriate sitting arrangement, learners are guided to discuss how to read plain scales. • In groups, learners are guided to identify drawings drawn to different scales using digital devices and visual aids. Ensure the visual aids are captioned or be provided with sign language interpretation. 29 • In purposive groups, learners are guided to practice drawing plane figures to a given plain scale.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Plain Scale Drawing in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Plain Scale Drawing together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Learning to Learn: learner acquires the skill to reflect on own work when practicing drawing of plane figures to a given

plain scale.

• Self-Efficacy: learner acquires intrinsic self-motivation when drawing plane figures to scale.

Values:
• Unity: learner enhances cooperation with peers when discussing how to read plain scales.

• Responsibility: learner demonstrates self-drive when practicing drawing plane figures to a given plain scale.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Peer education and mentorship: learner develops inter personal relationship and group dynamics skills while discussing

how to read plain scales.

Link to Other Subjects:

Mathematics: learner relates skills of scale drawing to linear scale in Mathematics.

Suggested learning resources

• Digital devices.

• Print and non-print media

• Pencils, chalk,

• Rulers, tape measures, carpenter’s tape measure

• Books, plain papers.

• Rubbers
